A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer OOD learnability framework and GROD algorithm. All 37 pages of v5 and 29 pages of v6, including appendices A–H, support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v5 reports original Gaussian-mixture experiments, image and text benchmark results, ResNet50 comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and visualizations.

after.justification: v6 reports original DINO-based image benchmark results alongside retained language-model and ResNet50 results, synthetic-data experiments, parameter studies, and visualizations.

M1.justification: The PCA/LDA outlier synthesis, Mahalanobis filtering, soft labels, combined classification loss, and VIM inference remain. The one-dimensional projection formulation matches v5's default num=1. Added warmup documentation does not establish that the underlying implementation changed.

E1.justification: v6 adds MNIST, Texture, and Places365 to the CIFAR OOD evaluations. For ImageNet-200, it replaces the CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100/SVHN evaluation with SSB-hard, NINCO, iNaturalist, Texture, and OpenImage-O. Auxiliary exposure datasets disappear with their comparison methods. The text tasks and Gaussian-mixture coverage remain.

E2.justification: OE, MIXOE, ATOM, POEM, and DIVOE are removed from both transformer and ResNet50 benchmark comparisons. OE and MIXOE also disappear from the runtime comparison. The remaining comparator families and the NLP comparator sets are retained; continued related-work citations do not constitute evaluation.

E3.justification: Appendix F replaces supervised ImageNet-1K-pretrained ViT-B-16 with self-supervised DINO using ViT-B-16. The stated image-training budget changes from 20 to 10 epochs and a from 0.001 to 0.1. Transformer evaluations drop ID accuracy from their reported metric set. Appendix D.2 also corrects the stated width factor w from 15 to 5 without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v5's projection-dimension sweep, generation-strategy and smoothing analyses, and module ablations for binary loss, synthetic outliers, and Mahalanobis filtering are removed, including Gaussian/uniform generation controls. v6 retains only two AUROC parameter sweeps for a and gamma in Figure 5. The Gaussian capacity study remains, while feature and likelihood visualizations are revised.

E5.justification: v5 states that each experiment is repeated five times with different random seeds; v6 removes this general disclosure. Figure 1 still reports five-seed results with standard deviations. This changes reporting completeness without establishing fewer experimental runs.

E6.justification: The main CV results are substantially replaced. For example, GROD's CIFAR-10 average FPR@95/AUROC changes from 0.12%/99.98% over three OOD datasets to 3.01%/99.33% over six with DINO; these are different-condition results, not a direct performance decline. NLP OOD scores and retained ResNet50 scores remain unchanged, while transformer ID-accuracy entries and removed comparators' results disappear.

T1.justification: Lemma C.5 adds the explicit assumption that labels are independent for classification, qualifying the existing probabilistic argument. The principal theorem statements, approximation bounds, and remaining proofs are substantially retained after renumbering Theorems 4.2/4.4/4.5 to 3.2/3.4/3.5.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: transformer OOD PAC learnability conditions, capacity-dependent approximation bounds, and theoretically motivated synthetic-outlier fine-tuning with strong image and text performance.

C2.justification: New Appendix H.4 acknowledges the absence of an established quantitative comparison of synthetic-outlier quality. Section 5 broadens compatibility wording from nearly all to all transformer architectures. Earlier explanations about supervised-pretraining overlap, projection artifacts, and several generation-strategy mechanisms are removed; the main non-overlap and architecture-specific theoretical limitations remain.

D1.justification: v6 newly documents initial warmup batches without L2 and updates training and hardware specifications. It removes the code-access paragraph and link, the gamma_opt=0.3 default, and the explicit best-ID-validation-accuracy checkpoint rule. These are disclosure changes; the missing link does not establish that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v6 adds DINO and new dataset references, plus recent OOD work by Regmi (2025) and Liu and Qin (2025). The Texture citation changes from Cimpoi et al. to a different work by Epperson et al. The central positioning relative to Fang's learnability framework and transformer approximation research remains.

P1.justification: The document substantially reorganizes its exposition: related work moves from Section 2 to Section 7, pseudocode and runtime discussion move into the main text, and the impact statement moves before the references. Experimental, dataset, and ablation narratives are extensively condensed or rewritten. The author list and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: v6 adopts a two-column main text, redraws the GROD overview and several plots, and reorganizes CV tables by metric and near/far-OOD groups. NLP tables lose ID-accuracy columns, the detailed ablation displays are replaced by two bar charts, and pseudocode and runtime figures receive more prominent placement.

improvement.justification: Broader DINO-based OOD evaluation and clearer displays improve coverage and accessibility, while the new synthetic-outlier-quality limitation improves qualification. However, removing component ablations, transformer ID-accuracy results, general seed reporting, and code-access information weakens validation and reproducibility. v6 also introduces a reporting error: Appendix G.1 calls 96.48% CIFAR-100 AUPR_IN, whereas Table 4 reports 89.27% AUPR_IN and 96.48% AUPR_OUT. These competing gains and losses do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
